newsitem.title: FINLAND: MERITA CEO SEES NO MAJOR COST PRESSURES.
newsitem.headline: MERITA CEO SEES NO MAJOR COST PRESSURES.

text.p: No significant cost pressures are in sight and it would be very hasty to start expecting trouble in the form of any excessive rise in prices, Merita chief executive Vesa Vainio said on Friday.
Growth had finally reached all major sectors of the economy, although many segments were still only in the stage of recovery, Vainio told a seminar according to a summary of a speech.
"In this situation it would be very hasty to start expecting that problems will start to pile up from the direction of an excessive rise in prices," Vainio said.
"No significant rising pressures are in sight in the cost trends," he said.
Referring to the coming autumn's collective bargaining, Vainio said everyone should remember that it only made sense to negotiate about the distribution of income after earnings had been generated.
"The bigger a national cake we can bake, the bigger can be the piece for each one," he said, adding the possibilities for Finland to raise living standards were good.
The European interest rate environment was calm and Finnish fiscal policy enjoyed confidence abroad, Vainio said.
